title: Checkpoint: The Deep
objective: After this level you can describe how animals survive the dark, cold and pressure of the deep.
summary: The deepest fish ever filmed swam at 8,336 m. Deep animals beat pressure by being mostly water, darkness with their own light or red bodies, and cold and hunger by going slow and big.

cards.headline: The deepest fish ever filmed was a baby.
cards.body: In 2022, a University of Western Australia and Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology team filmed a small juvenile snailfish at 8,336 m in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench off Japan. Let's use the whole chapter to explain how anything lives down there.

cards.headline: Pressure: be mostly water
cards.body: Level 9's foam cup shrank because air squeezes. Most deep-sea animals are largely water, which barely compresses, and many have no air-filled spaces, like lungs or swim bladders, to crush. Some animals even migrate 1,000 m up and down every day, through a 100-atmosphere swing, with no harm done. Their secret is having nothing to squash.

cards.headline: Darkness: make light, or vanish
cards.body: No sunlight reaches below 1,000 m, so many animals make their own: mostly blue bioluminescence, to escape, hide and hunt. Others hide by color. Red light never reaches the deep, so red animals look black and all but disappear.

cards.headline: Cold and hunger: go slow, think big
cards.body: The midnight zone holds a steady 4°C, and cold slows bodies down. Hunters like the anglerfish wait with a lure instead of chasing, many animals grow large to go farther between meals, and some neighborhoods skip sunlight entirely, living on whale bones and vent chemicals. The deep rewards patience.

cards.headline: Chapter 6 complete
learned: How deep-sea animals survive crushing pressure, total darkness, cold and scarce food.
Why so many deep-sea animals make their own light, and why most of it is blue.
How whole communities live without sunlight, on chemicals from vents and sunken whale bones.
Why so little of the deep has ever been seen, and why most of its species may still have no name.

questions.prompt: Deep recap: at what depth was the deepest fish ever filmed, a snailfish in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench in 2022?

options.label: About 1,000 m
About 4,000 m
options.rationale: That's the bottom of the midnight zone.

options.label: 10,935 m
options.rationale: That's Challenger Deep, the deepest point of the ocean.

questions.explanation: The juvenile snailfish was filmed at 8,336 m, the deepest fish on record.

questions.prompt: Deep recap: pressure crushes a foam cup's air pockets. Why doesn't it crush most deep-sea animals?

options.label: Their skin is too thick to squeeze
options.rationale: The key is what their bodies are made of.

options.label: They are mostly water, with no air spaces to crush
They swim up whenever pressure gets high
options.rationale: Some live their whole lives deep.

options.label: Pressure is lower in cold water

questions.explanation: Water barely compresses, and without lungs or swim bladders, deep animals have little for pressure to crush.

questions.prompt: Deep recap, from Level 51: in which depth zone was the snailfish filmed at 8,336 m?

options.label: The twilight zone
The midnight zone
The abyss
The hadal zone

questions.explanation: The hadal zone lies below 6,000 m, in the trenches, so 8,336 m is hadal.

questions.prompt: Deep recap, from Level 8: why are so many deep-sea animals red?

options.label: Red helps them soak up heat from the water
Red light glows brightest in deep water
options.rationale: Red light never reaches the deep.

options.label: No red light reaches, so red looks black
Red warns predators that they are poisonous

questions.explanation: Red light never reaches the deep, so red animals reflect nothing and look black.

questions.prompt: Deep recap, from Level 55: how does a deep-sea anglerfish get its meals while saving energy?

options.label: It waits with a glowing lure
It chases prey over long distances
options.rationale: That burns the energy it saves.

options.label: It eats marine snow from the floor
options.rationale: It's a hunter with a lure.

options.label: It farms microbes inside its body

questions.explanation: The anglerfish waits in the dark with a glowing lure instead of spending energy searching.
